It is the [[List of longest bridges above water in India|longest sea bridge]] in India, and the [[List of longest bridges|world's 12th longest sea bridge]].{{cite news|title=Mumbai To Navi Mumbai In 20 Minutes As India's Longest Sea Bridge Opens|url=https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/pm-inaugurates-mumbai-trans-harbour-link-indias-longest-sea-bridge-4848937|work=NDTV|date=12 January 2024|access-date=12 January 2024|language=en}}{{cite news|title=World's 12th Longest Sea Bridge In India|url=https://m.rediff.com/news/report/worlds-12th-longest-sea-bridge-in-india/20240108.html|work=Rediff News|date=8 January 2024|access-date=12 January 2024|language=en}} The bridge begins in [[Sewri]], [[South Mumbai]], crosses [[Thane Creek]] north of [[Elephanta Island]], and terminates at [[Chirle]] near [[Nhava Sheva]] in [[Uran taluka]], [[South Navi Mumbai]]. The road is linked to [[National Highway 348 (India)|NH348]] in the east and to the [[Eastern Freeway (Mumbai)|Eastern Freeway]] in the west. The 6-lane highway is 27 meters in width, in addition to two emergency exit lanes,{{cite web|title=Mumbai Trans Harbour Link expected to be built by 2021; Will it make your travel easier?|url=http://www.moneycontrol.com/news/business/companies/mumbai-trans-harbour-link-expected-to-be-built-by-2021-will-it-make-your-travel-easier-2443327.html|website=Moneycontrol|date=21 November 2017 |access-date=26 November 2017}} two edge strips, parallel crash barriers and noise barriers on both sides.{{cite web|url=http://dailypioneer.com/nation/123033-centre-sanctions-1920-cr-for-mumbai-trans-harbour-link-.html |title=The Pioneer |location=India |access-date=2013-07-21}}[http://www.cidcoindia.com/cidco/mthl.aspx] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120229040733/http://www.cidcoindia.com/cidco/mthl.aspx|date=29 February 2012}}{{cite news|url=http://www.indianexpress.com/news/trans-harbour-link-switches-tracks-to-metro/739683/ |title=Trans Harbour Link switches tracks to Metro |newspaper=[[The Indian Express]] |date=2011-01-20 |access-date=2013-07-21}} The project costs a total of {{INRConvert|17843|c}}. The bridge has a capacity to handle 70,000 vehicles per day.{{cite web |title=Mumbai may have to pay toll for 23 years to cruise on MTHL |url=https://www.dnaindia.com/mumbai/report-mumbai-may-have-to-pay-toll-for-23-years-to-cruise-on-mthl-2581267 |website=DNA India |access-date=15 October 2018 |date=4 February 2018}} Construction on the bridge began in April 2018, and was inaugurated by [[Prime Minister of India|Prime Minister]] [[Narendra Modi]] on 12 January 2024.{{cite news|title=PM Modi inaugurates India's longest sea bridge Atal Setu in Maharashtra|url=https://www.firstpost.com/india/pm-modi-inaugurates-indias-longest-sea-bridge-atal-setu-in-maharashtra-13606692.html|work=Firstpost|date=12 January 2024|access-date=12 January 2024|language=en}} ==Overview== [[File:PM inspecting the Atal Bihari Vajpayee Sewri-Nhava Sheva Atal Setu at Navi Mumbai, in Maharashtra on January 12, 2024.jpg|thumb|Prime minister inspecting the Atal Bihari Vajpayee Sewri-Nhava Sheva Atal Setu at Navi Mumbai, in Maharashtra on 12 January 2024]] In the 1990s, keeping the future of the [[Mumbai Metropolitan Region]] in mind, the [[Mumbai Metropolitan Region Development Authority]] (MMRDA) began studies on how to decongest the rising traffic and congestion in [[Mumbai]], and accidents and mishaps as their direct consequences. There are currently six bridges connecting Mumbai and [[Navi Mumbai]] across the [[Thane Creek]], but they are too narrow and outdated to handle future traffic. As a result, all of them are constrained and are carrying traffic beyond their limits, also increasing the commute time between the two cities. So, the MMRDA planned to build a comprehensive link between the two cities so as to handle more traffic and make travel easier, faster, safer, and hassle-free. The proposal was sent to the [[Government of Maharashtra]] for consideration in 2012. In 2015, the project was approved by the [[Government of India]] and the [[Ministry of Road Transport and Highways]] (MoRTH). Hence, the [[Cornerstone|foundation stone]] for the construction of the project was laid by [[Prime Minister of India|Prime Minister]] [[Narendra Modi]] on 24 December 2016. Initially, it was expected to be completed by 2021.{{cite news|title=Mumbai Trans Harbour Link: PM Narendra Modi lays foundation stone; 5 things to know about the mega project|url=https://www.financialexpress.com/india-news/mumbai-trans-harbour-link-5-things-to-know-about-the-project/485162/|work=The Financial Express|date=24 December 2016|access-date=5 January 2024|language=en}} Then, the MMRDA awarded contracts for the project in November 2017, and construction began in April 2018, which was scheduled to be completed within 4.5 years, by 2022. However, the construction was delayed by around 8 months due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]], and was expected to be completed by August 2023, then again by December 2023. The construction was finally completed in December 2023 and was inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on 12 January 2024.{{cite news|title=Atal Setu: PM Modi Inaugurates India's Longest Sea Bridge In Maharashtra|url=https://zeenews.india.com/india/atal-setu-pm-modi-inaugurates-indias-longest-sea-bridge-in-maharashtra-2709012.html|work=Zee News|date=12 January 2024|access-date=12 January 2024|language=en}} ==Planning== [[File:Mumbai trans Harbor link.jpg|thumb|Mumbai trans Harbor link map]] Transportation and traffic planning for [[Mumbai Metropolitan Region|Greater Bombay]] (now [[Mumbai]]) was commissioned to [[CDM Smith#History|Wilbur Smith and Associates]] (WSA) (now ([[CDM Smith]]) in mid-1962. The firm's report, based on extensive studies conducted over 18 months, was handed over to the [[Ministry of Road Transport and Highways]] (MoRTH) on 19 December 1963. Among other projects, the report proposed the construction of a sea link, known as the Uran Bridge, to connect Mumbai with the mainland near the town of [[Uran]]. However, WSA was unsure of the link's feasibility. Citing poor traffic expectations in Uran even in 1981, WSA's report advised a more detailed study of this connection and recommended to delay the link until development and community services are expanded in the Trans-[[Thane]] region.{{cite news|last=Shukla|first=Alka|title=The man who saw tomorrow...|url=http://www.mumbaimirror.com/mumbai/others/The-man-who-saw-tomorrow--/articleshow/16111678.cms|access-date=31 March 2014|newspaper=Mumbai Mirror|date=22 March 2011|location=Mumbai}} In 1973, the [[Vashi Bridge]] linking [[Mankhurd]] in Mumbai with [[Vashi]] in [[Navi Mumbai]] was opened. ===First attempt=== The first concrete attempt to build the sea link was made in 2004, when [[Infrastructure Leasing & Financial Services]] (IL&FS) submitted a proposal to implement the project on a [[Build–operate–transfer|build, own, operate, and transfer]] (BOOT) basis. The [[Maharashtra State Road Development Corporation]] (MSRDC) also submitted a counter-proposal. However, the IL&FS proposal was sidelined by the [[Government of Maharashtra]] for undisclosed reasons.{{Cite web | url=http://www.moneylife.in/article/sewri-nhava-sheva-trans-harbour-link-the-story-of-unrealistic-bidding-and-spiralling-cost/33729.html | title=Sewri-Nhava Sheva Trans-Harbour Link: The story of unrealistic bidding and spiralling cost}} ===Second attempt=== Another attempt was made in 2005, when the MSRDC invited bids for the project. The bids submitted by the [[Ambani]] brothers were considered to be unrealistic.{{cite news|agency=Press Trust of India|url=http://articles.economictimes.indiatimes.com/2011-10-25/news/30320332_1_metro-rail-projects-mmrda-commissioner-rahul-asthana-mthl |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120603132157/http://articles.economictimes.indiatimes.com/2011-10-25/news/30320332_1_metro-rail-projects-mmrda-commissioner-rahul-asthana-mthl |url-status=dead |archive-date=3 June 2012 |title=World Bank may fund Mumbai Trans Harbour Link project |newspaper=[[The Economic Times]] |date=2011-10-25 |access-date=2013-07-21}} A consortium of the [[Anil Dhirubhai Ambani Group]], [[Reliance Infrastructure|Reliance Energy]] (REL), and [[Hyundai Engineering & Construction]] quoted a concession period of nine years and 11 months, against 75 years quoted by [[Mukesh Ambani]]'s Sea King Infrastructure (the only other shortlisted bidder left, after [[Larsen & Toubro]]-[[Gammon India|Gammon]] and [[IFFCO]] opted out). The REL-Hyundai consortium was initially disqualified at the technical bid stage, as Hyundai did not meet the criteria of $200 million net worth specified in the bid document. However, the consortium challenged the disqualification in the [[Supreme Court of India|Supreme Court]], and the Court granted them 90 days to submit their bid that ended on 15 December 2007. The consortium eventually won the bid in February 2008.{{Cite news | url=http://www.business-standard.com/article/economy-policy/anil-trounces-mukesh-in-bidding-for-mumbai-sea-link-project-108022101002_1.html | title=Anil trounces Mukesh in bidding for Mumbai sea link project| newspaper=Business Standard| date=21 February 2008}} However, the MSRDC was not sure about the viability of the low concession period. The MSRDC felt that the concession periods were "unrealistic" and that both bids "seemed frivolous in nature". ===Third attempt=== The [[Government of Maharashtra]] called for fresh bids for the project in 2008. However, none of the 13 companies that had shown interest submitted bids. The media criticized the political feud between the ruling [[Nationalist Congress Party]] (NCP) and the [[Indian National Congress]] coalition, as being responsible for "slowing down the pace of Mumbai's development". The city's two infrastructure agencies, the MSRDC and the [[Mumbai Metropolitan Region Development Authority]] (MMRDA), under the NCP and Congress respectively, were both planning to construct the Mumbai Trans Harbour Link (MTHL) at the same time. The project underwent two failed rounds of tendering under the MSRDC and was stuck for nearly two years (between 2009 and 2011) before the state government decided to hand over the mandate to MMRDA. Following the decision, the MSRDC asked MMRDA to pay {{INRConvert|25|c}} if it wanted access to any of the studies on the project conducted by the former. After the MMRDA was tasked with executing the MTHL, the MSRDC took up the expansion of the [[Vashi Bridge]] by adding six more lanes to ease congestion at the entrance to Navi Mumbai. However, the MMRDA refused the MSRDC's request to allocate funds for the expansion of the Vashi Bridge, as the former believed that the expansion would divert some ridership from the MTHL.{{Cite web |date=2013-07-05 |title=Rift between Cong, NCP ministers slows down Mumbai infra projects |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/news-archive/web/rift-between-cong-ncp-ministers-slows-down-mumbai-infra-projects/ |access-date=2023-07-01 |website=The Indian Express |language=en}} ===Fourth attempt=== The MMRDA appointed [[Arup Group|Arup Consultancy Engineers]] and [[KPMG]] to conduct the techno-economic feasibility study of the MTHL in August 2011. The MTHL project was proposed as a [[public–private partnership]] (PPP) model.{{cite web|url=http://daily.bhaskar.com/article/MAH-MUM-mumbai-trans-harbour-link-mmrda-to-invite-bids-in-november-2416330.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141029004854/http://daily.bhaskar.com/article/MAH-MUM-mumbai-trans-harbour-link-mmrda-to-invite-bids-in-november-2416330.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=29 October 2014 |title=Mumbai Trans Harbour Link MMRDA to invite bids in November |publisher=daily.bhaskar.com |access-date=2013-07-21}} The project received clearance from the then [[Chief Minister of Maharashtra]], [[Prithviraj Chavan]], on 22 October 2012.{{cite news|url=http://www.hindustantimes.com/India-news/Mumbai/Mumbai-trans-harbour-sea-link-cleared/Article1-948884.aspx |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121023093131/http://www.hindustantimes.com/India-news/Mumbai/Mumbai-trans-harbour-sea-link-cleared/Article1-948884.aspx |url-status=dead |archive-date=23 October 2012 |title=Mumbai trans-harbour sea-link cleared |newspaper=[[Hindustan Times]] |date=2012-10-23 |access-date=2013-07-21}} ''[[The Times of India]]'' described the MTHL's delay as being "symbolic of all that is wrong with infrastructure planning and implementation in Mumbai." The newspaper daily also stated that a project being "on the drawing board after more than forty years would be in the realm of fiction in any other country".{{cite web |title=State may go it alone in trans-harbour project |url=http://epaper.timesofindia.com/Default/Scripting/ArticleWin.asp?From=Archive&Source=Page&Skin=TOINEW&BaseHref=TOIM%2F2013%2F07%2F21&ViewMode=GIF&PageLabel=2&EntityId=Ar00200&AppName=1 |website=Times of India |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304112327/http://epaper.timesofindia.com/Default/Scripting/ArticleWin.asp?From=Archive&Source=Page&Skin=TOINEW&BaseHref=TOIM%2F2013%2F07%2F21&ViewMode=GIF&PageLabel=2&EntityId=Ar00200&AppName=1|date=21 June 2013 |archive-date=4 March 2016 |url-status=dead}} The project received environmental clearance from the [[Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change]] (MoEFCC) on 23 October 2012. The [[Maharashtra State Road Development Corporation]] (MSRDC) had obtained clearance for the project in March 2005, but the certificate was valid only for 5 years and lapsed due to the delays in the bidding process. The ministry laid down 11 conditions that the MMRDA had to follow. Some of the conditions were that the MMRDA had to put up noise barriers, replant five times the number of mangroves destroyed, not carry out dredging or reclamation, use construction equipment with exhaust silencers, and work in consultation with the [[Bombay Natural History Society]] to minimize the impact on migratory birds.{{cite news|url=http://www.hindustantimes.com/India-news/Mumbai/Centre-may-finance-20-of-the-cost-of-trans-harbour-link/Article1-952503.aspx|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141028222627/http://www.hindustantimes.com/India-news/Mumbai/Centre-may-finance-20-of-the-cost-of-trans-harbour-link/Article1-952503.aspx|url-status=dead|archive-date=28 October 2014|title=Centre may finance 20% of the cost of trans-harbour link|newspaper=[[Hindustan Times]]|date=31 October 2012|access-date=2012-10-31}}{{cite web|url=http://www.financialexpress.com/news/sewrinhava-link-crz-clearance-bid-gets-central-government-push/1022228/0 |title=Sewri-Nhava link CRZ clearance bid gets central government push |work=The Financial Express |date=2012-10-26 |access-date=2013-07-21}}{{cite web|title=BNHS to monitor impact of MTHL bridge on flamingos|url=http://indianexpress.com/article/mumbai/bnhs-to-monitor-impact-of-mthl-bridge-on-flamingos-4599895/|website=The Indian Express|access-date=6 April 2017|date=5 April 2017}} Environmental activists were opposed to the clearance. They pointed out that there was no public hearing following the second application for environmental clearance. They still believe that the sea link is not allowed as per the new [[Coastal Regulation Zone]] (CRZ) notification of 2011. They also claim that the sea link would damage a huge mudflat and mangrove tract towards [[Sewri]] and [[Nhava Sheva]], which is a habitat for migratory birds like flamingos.{{cite news|author=Chittaranjan Tembhekar |agency=TNN |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/mumbai/Shot-in-arm-for-Mumbai-Trans-Harbour-Link-as-project-gets-environment-ministrys-nod/articleshow/16934369.cms |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130126081108/http://articles.timesofindia.indiatimes.com/2012-10-24/mumbai/34707528_1_fresh-application-sewri-and-nhava-environmental-clearance |url-status=live |archive-date=2013-01-26 |title=Shot in arm for Mumbai Trans-Harbour Link as project gets environment ministry's nod | newspaper=[[The Times of India]] |date=2012-10-24 |access-date=2013-07-21}} Nevertheless, the MMRDA finalised the plan to construct sound barriers on the bridge so that it does not affect the flamingo habitat at Sewri. The [[Department of Atomic Energy]] (DAE) had directed MMRDA to construct a six-km long view barrier to cut the view of [[Bhabha Atomic Research Centre]] (BARC).{{cite web|title=MMRDA gets final nod for trans-harbour link project|url=http://www.mumbaimirror.com/mumbai/others/MMRDA-gets-final-nod-for-trans-harbour-link-project/articleshow/18087483.cms|work=[[Mumbai Mirror]]|access-date=21 July 2013|author=Yogesh Naik|date=19 January 2013}} The MTHL received coastal regulation zone clearance from the MoEFCC on 19 July 2013.{{Cite web | url=http://www.dnaindia.com/mumbai/1881768/report-mthl-bridge-finally-gets-crz-approval-from-centre |title = MTHL bridge finally gets CRZ approval from Centre|date = 30 August 2013}} On 31 October 2012, the [[Ministry of Finance (India)#Department of Economic Affairs|Department of Economic Affairs]] (DEA) granted in-principle approval for the MTHL.{{cite news|url=http://www.hindustantimes.com/India-news/Mumbai/Trans-harbour-link-gets-centre-funding-boost/Article1-952493.aspx |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121030212414/http://www.hindustantimes.com/India-news/Mumbai/Trans-harbour-link-gets-centre-funding-boost/Article1-952493.aspx |url-status=dead |archive-date=30 October 2012 |title=Trans-harbour link gets centre funding boost |newspaper=Hindustan Times |date=2012-10-31 |access-date=2013-07-21}} The DEA recommended granting {{INRConvert|1920|c}} with a concession period of 35 years for the project.{{cite web|url=http://www.dnaindia.com/mumbai/report_centre-approves-mthl-funding_1758221 |title=Centre approves MTHL funding – Mumbai – DNA |work=Daily News and Analysis|date= 31 October 2012|access-date=2013-07-21}} In the first meeting, between MMRDA and DEA officials in September 2012, the ministry had asked the authority to treat the sea link as a road and reduce the proposed concession period from 45 years to 30 years. They also expected an internal rate of return of 15% for the project. However, the MMRDA wanted a higher rate as they claimed the project was very risky. An internal rate of return of 17% was agreed upon. The termination clause in the concession agreement comes into effect after 30 years into the concession period. The MMRDA can invoke the clause based on certain conditions, such as the capacity being higher than expected. The conditions will be reviewed in the 20th year of the concession agreement.{{cite news|url=http://www.indianexpress.com/news/mumbai-harbour-link-funding-gets-finmin-nod/1024287/0 |title=Mumbai harbour link funding gets FinMin nod |newspaper=The Indian Express|date=2012-10-31 |access-date=2013-07-21}} The DEA is the first tier of the three-tier clearance process to get [[viability gap funding]] (VGF) for the project. The project must also receive approval from an empowered committee and finally from the [[Minister of Finance (India)|Finance Minister]]. On 9 November 2012, the State Government issued a state-support agreement and a toll notification for the project.{{cite news|agency=TNN |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/mumbai/MTHL-toll-fixed-before-work-starts/articleshow/17162858.cms |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130103074303/http://articles.timesofindia.indiatimes.com/2012-11-10/mumbai/35033542_1_sea-link-toll-amounts-mthl |url-status=live |archive-date=2013-01-03 |title=MTHL toll fixed before work starts |newspaper=[[The Times of India]] |date=2012-11-10 |access-date=2013-07-21}} The empowered committee approved VGF for MTHL on 12 December 2012.{{cite news|url=http://www.indianexpress.com/news/mumbai-transharbour-link-a-step-away-from-becoming-reality/1044511/0 |title=Mumbai Trans-Harbour Link a step away from becoming reality |newspaper=[[The Indian Express]] |date=2012-12-13 |access-date=2013-07-21}} The then Finance Minister, [[P. Chidambaram]], cleared the project on 18 January 2013.{{cite web|url=http://www.dnaindia.com/mumbai/report_mmrda-puts-mthl-corridor-on-fast-track_1793708 |title=MMRDA puts MTHL corridor on fast track |work=Daily News and Analysis|date=2013-01-29 |access-date=2013-07-21}}{{cite news|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/mumbai/MTHL-set-to-take-off-with-1920cr-boost-from-Centre/articleshow/18083927.cms |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130411040843/http://articles.timesofindia.indiatimes.com/2013-01-19/mumbai/36431174_1_heavy-vehicles-chirle-mthl |url-status=live |archive-date=2013-04-11 |title=MTHL set to take off with 1,920cr boost from Centre |newspaper=[[The Times of India]] |date=2013-01-19 |access-date=2013-07-21}}{{cite news|url=http://www.hindustantimes.com/India-news/Mumbai/Central-funds-for-sea-bridge-work-to-begin-by-year-end/Article1-993180.aspx |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130119145111/http://www.hindustantimes.com/India-news/Mumbai/Central-funds-for-sea-bridge-work-to-begin-by-year-end/Article1-993180.aspx |url-status=dead |archive-date=19 January 2013 |title=Central funds for sea bridge, work to begin by year-end |newspaper=[[Hindustan Times]] |date=2013-01-19 |access-date=2013-07-21}} The [[Jawaharlal Nehru Port Trust]] (JNPT) asked the MMRDA to build the MTHL at a height of 51 metres, instead of the proposed 25 metres, for a span of 300 metres to accommodate its expansion plans for its fifth container terminal and to allow safe passage of bigger vessels. MMRDA expressed that a height of 51 metres would not be feasible as it would have a huge impact on the cost. The project requires clearance from the ministry as it will affect 38 hectares of protected mangrove forests and 8.8 hectares of forest land on the Navi Mumbai end. The sea link's starting point poses a threat to an estimated 20,000–30,000 lesser and greater flamingos and the mangrove habitat. The Sewri mudflats are home to 150 species of birds, and are listed as an "Important Bird Area". The FAC instructed the state government to submit a study report on the project's impact on the flamingo population, and recommended that the government seek the help of either the [[Bombay Natural History Society]] (BNHS) or the [[Wildlife Institute of India]], [[Dehradun]], to conduct the study. The cost of the study would be borne by the MMRDA, which would also have to come with safeguards to cause the least disturbance to the flamingos at Sewri. On 17 April 2015, the Minister of Road Transport and Highways, [[Nitin Gadkari]], stated that he favoured the construction of a submarine tunnel instead of a sea link. November 2017, the MMRDA awarded contracts to a consortium of [[Larsen & Toubro]] (L&T) and Japan's [[IHI Corporation]], a consortium of [[Daewoo]] and [[Tata Projects]] (TPL), and L&T itself to construct the Sewri side of the sea bridge, the Navi Mumbai side of the sea bridge, and the bridge portion on land towards Chirle, respectively.{{cite web|title=MMRDA appoints three contractors for MTHL|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/mumbai/mmrda-appoints-three-contractors-for-mthl/articleshow/61584848.cms|website=The Times of India|access-date=9 November 2017}} The contracts between the MMRDA and the L&T-IHI Corporation consortium were officially signed on 27 December 2017. L&T was awarded {{INRConvert|7637.3|c}} for the 10.38 km package 1 and {{INRConvert|1013.79|c}} for the 3.61 km package 3. The contract for the 7.807 km package 2 was signed with Daewoo and Tata Projects at a cost of {{INRConvert|5612.61|c}} at a later date.{{cite news|last1=Mahale|first1=Ajeet|title=Pact signed to execute MTHL|url=http://www.thehindu.com/news/cities/mumbai/pact-signed-to-execute-mthl/article22282745.ece|newspaper=The Hindu|access-date=11 May 2018|language=en-IN|date=27 December 2017}}{{cite web|title=MMRDA signs pacts for construction of MTHL packages|url=https://www.moneycontrol.com/news/business/mmrda-signs-pacts-for-construction-of-mthl-packages-2469271.html|website=Moneycontrol|date=27 December 2017 |access-date=11 May 2018}} The MMRDA invited bids for Package 4 in September 2021. The tender includes the design, supply, installation, testing, and commissioning of an [[intelligent transport system]], toll management, highway and bridge street lighting, electrical works, construction of toll plazas, and administrative buildings.{{Cite web|date=2021-09-05|title=MTHL project: MMRDA invites bids for construction of 'Package 4'|url=https://indianexpress.com/article/cities/mumbai/mthl-project-mmrda-invites-bids-for-construction-of-package-4-7489269/|access-date=2021-11-25|website=The Indian Express|language=en}} The {{INRConvert|427|c}} contract for Package 4 was awarded to a joint venture between Strabag Infrastructure & Safety Solutions GmbH and Strabag AG, both owned by the [[Austria]]n construction company, [[Strabag]]. {| class="wikitable" |+ !Package !Length !Details !Contractor(s) !Cost |- |1 |10.38 km |Bridge portion across Thane Creek, and the Sewri [[Interchange (road)#T and Y interchanges|Y-interchange]]. |[[Larsen & Toubro]] and [[IHI Corporation]] |{{INRConvert|7637.3|c}} |- |2 |7.807 km |Bridge portion across Thane Creek, and the Shivaji Nagar [[cloverleaf interchange]]. |[[Tata Projects]] Limited and [[Daewoo E&C]] |{{INRConvert|5612.61|c}} |- |3 |3.613 km |Viaducts and interchanges that connect MTHL with State Highways 52 and 54 and National Highway 4B at Chirle. |Larsen & Toubro |{{INRConvert|1013.79|c}} |- |4 |{{n/a}} |[[Intelligent transport system]], toll management, street lighting, electrical works, toll plazas, and administrative buildings. |[[Strabag]]{{Cite web |date=2023-01-02 |title=MTHL: Modern bridge technology used to overcome challenges at sea |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/cities/mumbai/mthl-modern-bridge-technology-overcome-challenges-sea-8356824/ |access-date=2023-07-01 |website=The Indian Express |language=en}} |{{INRConvert|526|c}} |} === Land acquisition === The project required 130 hectares of land. The [[City and Industrial Development Corporation]] (CIDCO) contributed 88 hectares. The remaining land was privately owned.{{cite news|url=http://www.indianexpress.com/news/port-trust-consent-to-unlock-80--land-for-mthl-project/1046262/0 |title=Port Trust consent to unlock 80% land for MTHL project |newspaper=[[The Indian Express]] |date=2012-12-17 |access-date=2013-07-21}} According to MMRDA officials, land owners were given the same compensation package as that given in the [[Navi Mumbai International Airport]] project.{{cite web|author=Rahul Wadke |url=http://www.thehindubusinessline.com/companies/jnpt-to-pick-up-stake-in-mumbai-trans-harbour-link/article6112180.ece |title=JNPT to pick up stake in Mumbai Trans Harbour Link | Business Line |website=Business Line |date=2014-06-13 |access-date=2016-01-21}} Three hundred and twenty structures in Sewri were affected by the project, of which 250 properties were residential. The MMRDA provided resettlement for the affected people by offering accommodation in either [[Kanjurmarg]] or [[Kurla]]. The majority chose to relocate to Kanjurmarg.{{cite news|author= |title=MMRDA begins allotment of houses for MTHL project displaced in Sewri|url=http://www.thehindu.com/news/cities/mumbai/mmrda-begins-allotment-of-houses-for-mthl-project-displaced-in-sewri/article23650994.ece|newspaper=The Hindu|access-date=11 May 2018|language=en-IN|date=23 April 2018}} The MMRDA also paid {{INRConvert|6|l}} each as compensation to 1,500 fishermen who were affected by the construction of the project.{{cite web |title=Mumbai Trans-Harbour Link Corridor: New survey on cards to identify more affected fishermen |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/cities/mumbai/mumbai-trans-harbour-link-corridor-new-survey-on-cards-to-identify-more-affected-fishermen-5545693/ |website=The Indian Express |access-date=26 January 2019 |language=en-IN |date=19 January 2019}} In October 2016, the MMRDA agreed to pay MbPT a total of {{INR}}1000 crores in installments over the course of 30 years, as rent for using the MbPT's land for construction of ramps for the MTHL on the Mumbai side.{{cite news|title=Mumbai Port Trust to free 150 hectares for infrastructure projects – The Economic Times|url=http://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/transportation/shipping-/-transport/mumbai-port-trust-to-free-150-hectares-for-infrastructure-projects/articleshow/54856910.cms|newspaper=The Economic Times|access-date=14 October 2016|date=14 October 2016|last1=Babar|first1=Kailash}}{{cite web|title=MMRDA resolves port land acquisition issue to construct MTHL|url=http://www.hindustantimes.com/mumbai-news/mmrda-resolves-port-land-acquisition-issue-to-construct-mthl/story-X4gAd5hRbkeriil7K7ZyIJ.html|website=Hindustan Times|access-date=14 October 2016|date=11 October 2016}} The MMRDA received 27.2 hectares of land on the Sewri side of the MbPT, of which 15.17 hectares were temporarily used for the casting yard.{{Cite web | url=http://indianexpress.com/article/cities/mumbai/mumbai-trans-harbour-link-to-receive-land-for-casting-yard-soon-4735987/ |title = Mumbai Trans Harbour Link to receive land for casting yard soon|date = 5 July 2017}} The MMRDA utilized drones to carry out survey work for the MTHL. The drones were fitted with 360-degree cameras that provide up to 3 mm accuracy. The aerial survey takes less time than a regular survey, achieves greater accuracy and helps protect against false claims for compensation.{{cite web|title=MMRDA plans drone survey for other Metro lines|url=http://indianexpress.com/article/cities/mumbai/mmrda-plans-drone-survey-for-other-metro-lines/|website=The Indian Express|access-date=7 March 2017|date=7 March 2017}} Over 1,000 boreholes were drilled to study the strata.{{cite web|title=Mumbai Trans-Harbour Link project work gathers pace|url=http://www.thehindubusinessline.com/economy/logistics/mumbai-transharbour-link-project-work-gathers-pace/article9618081.ece|website=Business Line|access-date=6 April 2017|language=en|date=5 April 2017}} The MMRDA began conducting a geological survey for the project on 15 January 2018.{{cite web|title=Construction work of Mumbai Trans Harbour Link to begin from next month|url=http://www.freepressjournal.in/mumbai/construction-work-of-mumbai-trans-harbour-link-to-begin-from-next-month/1222898|website=Free Press Journal|access-date=19 February 2018|date=17 February 2018}} The project work affected 1,635 trees, of which 753 were cut, and the remaining 882 were replanted at other locations. Most of the affected trees were located at Sewri and [[Vakola]].{{cite web |title=753 trees set to be axed for infrastructure; send objections soon |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/mumbai-news/753-trees-set-to-be-axed-for-infra-send-objections-soon/story-vO0weRlK0kXPESUNKlj6cP.html |website=Hindustan Times |access-date=23 September 2019 |language=en |date=16 August 2019}}{{cite news |last1=Mahale |first1=Ajeet |title=BMC gets public support for MTHL, but not for tree felling |url=https://www.thehindu.com/news/cities/mumbai/bmc-gets-public-support-for-mthl-but-not-for-tree-felling/article29226770.ece |newspaper=The Hindu |access-date=23 September 2019 |language=en-IN |date=23 August 2019}} ===Metro line=== In 2010, the MMRDA appointed [[Rail India Technical and Economic Service]] (RITES) to prepare a [[Project plan|detailed project report]] (DPR) for the Mumbai Trans Harbour Metro Rail Link (MTHMRL), a proposal to build a dual-track metro line under the road lanes of the MTHL. The 49-km long metro line was proposed to connect [[Prabhadevi]] and Dushmi, about 20 km away from Chirle.{{Cite web |date=2022-03-08 |title=MMRDA revives plan to build Metro corridor on MTHL, feasibility report awaited |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/cities/mumbai-news/mmrda-revives-plan-to-build-metro-corridor-on-mthl-feasibility-report-awaited-101646745977861.html |access-date=2023-07-01 |website=Hindustan Times |language=en}} The metro line was to be extended to the proposed [[Navi Mumbai International Airport]], and connected to the proposed [[Ranjanpada railway station|Ranjanpada]]-[[Seawoods–Darave railway station|Seawoods]]-[[Kharkopar railway station|Kharkopar]] corridor of the [[Navi Mumbai Metro]] and the proposed Sewri-Prabhadevi corridor of the [[Mumbai Metro]]. However, the MMRDA scrapped plans for the metro line in 2012 and decided to build only a road bridge. An MMRDA official stated that a detailed study has revealed that laying the foundation for the bridge with provisions for two metro lines would hike costs, instead of saving expenses. Hence, it would be feasible to have a separate bridge for the metro in the future. Another reason given was that the Navi Mumbai International Airport and Sewri-Prabhadevi corridor of the Mumbai Metro were still a long way from completion.{{cite web |date=2012-06-05 |title=Govt scraps metro line on trans harbour link |url=http://www.dnaindia.com/mumbai/report_govt-scraps-metro-line-on-trans-harbour-link_1698194 |access-date=2013-07-21 |work=Daily News and Analysis}} In June 2021, the MMRDA stated that it was re-examining the possibility of building metro lines on the MTHL. An official stated that there would be no need for extra construction on the MTHL for the metro line, as only the tracks would have to be added. Already, the Worli–Sewri underground metro corridor, as part of the [[Line 3 (Mumbai Metro)|Line 3 (Aqua Line)]] of [[Mumbai Metro]], is being constructed. The Sewri metro station will connect the MTHL through access paths, thereby linking it to Navi Mumbai.{{Cite web |date=2021-06-20 |title=Mumbai: MMRDA examines possibility of constructing Metro corridor on MTHL |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/cities/mumbai/mmrda-examines-possibility-of-constructing-metro-corridor-on-mthl-7366838/ |access-date=2021-11-25 |website=The Indian Express |language=en}} In September 2021, the MMRDA stated that regardless of the decision on metro lines, the agency would dedicate two lanes on the MTHL for a [[bus rapid transit]] system.{{Cite web |title=Mumbai: Plan for dedicated bus lane on MTHL |url=https://www.freepressjournal.in/mumbai/mumbai-plan-for-dedicated-bus-lane-on-mthl |access-date=2021-11-25 |website=Free Press Journal |language=en}} The agency appointed a consultant to determine whether metro lines could be constructed on the MTHL in January 2022. The draft report of the study submitted in April 2022 found that the MTHL's existing pillars would not be able to support the load of a metro system. The then Metropolitan Commissioner of the MMRDA, S.V.R. Srinivas, stated that the agency was exploring solutions, such as increasing the load bearing capacity of the pillars, before making a final decision.{{Cite web |date=2022-04-04 |title=MTHL won't be able to bear load of Metro: Report |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/cities/mumbai-news/mthl-won-t-be-able-to-bear-load-of-metro-report-101649080892977.html |access-date=2022-05-03 |website=Hindustan Times |language=en}} ==Construction== [[File:MTHL work from Sewri Fort.jpg|upright=1.25|thumb|MTHL under construction on the Sewri side, March 2021]] The MTHL is 21.8 km long, including 16.5 km sea bridge and 5.5 km of viaducts on land on either end of the bridge.{{cite web|url=http://www.dnaindia.com/mumbai/report_30-year-evil-spell-on-trans-harbour-link-ends_1664623 |title=30-year evil spell on trans-harbour link ends |work=Daily News and Analysis|date=2012-03-20 |access-date=2013-07-21}} It was constructed in three sections.{{cite web|title=MMRDA's 20-year MTHL dream to be reality soon|url=http://www.mid-day.com/articles/mmrdas-20-year-mthl-dream-to-be-reality-soon/17641157|website=mid-day|access-date=14 October 2016|date=26 September 2016}} Construction of the bridge required the use of 165,000 tonnes of [[reinforcement steel]], 96,250 tonnes of [[structural steel]], and 830,000 cubic metres of [[concrete]]. The bridge features the first use of [[orthotropic deck]]s in India. The special steel decks enable the bridge to have longer spans than possible with regular girders.{{Cite web|last=Phadke|first=Manasi|date=2021-11-24|title=A first in India: Mumbai Trans-Harbour Link to have special decks to make longer-span bridge|url=https://theprint.in/india/a-first-in-india-mumbai-trans-harbour-link-to-have-special-decks-to-make-longer-span-bridge/770609/|access-date=2021-11-26|website=ThePrint|language=en-US}} A total of 70 orthotropic decks were used on the bridge, requiring about 96,250 tonnes of steel.{{Cite web |date=2021-10-11 |title=Mumbai: Bridging the bay |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/cities/mumbai/mumbai-bridging-the-bay-trans-harbour-link-7564451/ |access-date=2022-12-06 |website=The Indian Express |language=en}} The steel spans weigh up to 2,600 tonnes and make up 4.7 km of the bridge length, while the rest of the bridge is made up of 60 metre-long concrete spans weighing up to 130 tonnes each.{{Cite news |date=2023-04-16 |title=More than 90% of Mumbai Trans-Harbour Link was assembled before installation at site |work=The Times of India |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/mumbai/more-than-90-of-mumbai-trans-harbour-link-was-assembled-before-installation-at-site/articleshow/99527378.cms?from=mdr |access-date=2023-07-01 |issn=0971-8257}} This 4.7 km section sits at the highest point of the MTHL and includes a 180-metre-long steel span, which is the longest steel span in India. The shortest steel span on the MTHL is 110 meters long. The MMRDA chose to use steel spans in these sections to eliminate the need to construct pillars to support the bridge, which would hinder the movement of ships in the area.{{cite web |title=Mumbai Trans Harbour Link to have longest steel deck in country |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/cities/mumbai/mthl-to-have-longest-steel-deck-in-country-5179718/ |website=The Indian Express |access-date=15 October 2018|date=17 May 2018 }}{{cite web |title=Longest steel span for MTHL |url=http://www.asianage.com/metros/mumbai/160518/longest-steel-span-for-mthl.html |website=The Asian Age |access-date=15 October 2018 |date=16 May 2018}} Only about 3% of the bridge structure was built on-site, including the foundations and pouring cement over metal girders. The rest of the bridge was pre-fabricated and then transported to the construction site for installation. The parts for the orthotropic decks were manufactured in Japan, [[Myanmar]], [[Taiwan]], and [[Vietnam]] and shipped to Karanja Port in Uran for assembly. The decks were carried to the construction site by barge, and each deck required about 3 days to install in place. A programmed self-propelled transporter was utilized to load the deck onto the barge, and computer-controlled jacks were utilized to install it on the bridge within a precision band of 5 mm. The barge used to transport the decks was specifically built for the MTHL project by [[Larsen & Toubro]] at its [[Kattupalli Shipyard]].{{Cite web |title=First Orthotropic Steel Deck (OSD) Erected in Package 1 of JICA funded 'The Mumbai Trans Harbour Link (MTHL) Bridge project' {{!}} India {{!}} Countries & Regions {{!}} JICA |url=https://www.jica.go.jp/Resource/india/english/office/topics/press220114.html |access-date=2023-07-01 |website=www.jica.go.jp}} The concrete section of the bridge is made up of over 12,000 concrete boxes that were pre-cast in a casting yard. The concrete segments were joined to form 60 metre-long spans, and the concrete spans were then installed on the bridge's pillars using a mobile gantry. The foundations for the MTHL are 47 metres at its deepest points, to support the weight of the bridge.{{Cite web|date=2021-10-11|title=Mumbai: Bridging the bay|url=https://indianexpress.com/article/cities/mumbai/mumbai-bridging-the-bay-trans-harbour-link-7564451/|access-date=2021-11-25|website=The Indian Express|language=en}} An automated girder launching system was utilized to lay the bridge's foundation, marking the first time the system was used in India.{{Cite news|last=Gajara|first=Dhairya|date=2020-01-17|title=Uddhav launches first MTHL girder|language=en-IN|work=The Hindu|url=https://www.thehindu.com/news/cities/mumbai/uddhav-launches-first-mthl-girder/article30580087.ece|access-date=2021-11-25|issn=0971-751X}} The Reverse Circulation Drilling (RCD) construction technique was also utilized for the first time in India, to reduce disturbance to migratory birds.{{Cite web |last=Phadke |first=Manasi |date=2023-01-13 |title=How India's longest sea link is taking shape in Mumbai one span at a time & notching many firsts |url=https://theprint.in/india/governance/how-indias-longest-sea-link-is-taking-shape-in-mumbai-one-span-at-a-time-notching-many-firsts/1310929/ |access-date=2023-07-01 |website=ThePrint |language=en-US}} The MMRDA estimated that the construction work would generate 115,419 man-months of employment.{{Cite web|title=About 35% of Mumbai Trans Harbour Sealink project cost spent so far|url=https://www.freepressjournal.in/mumbai/about-35-of-mumbai-trans-harbor-sealink-project-cost-spent-so-far|access-date=2021-11-25|website=Free Press Journal|language=en}} Over 14,000 workers were involved throughout the construction of the MTHL. Contractors worked round-the-clock in three 8-hour shifts. Expert consultants from 10 different countries including [[Brazil]], Denmark, Japan, South Korea, Switzerland, the United Kingdom, the United States, and some [[Middle East|Middle Eastern astern]] countries, were involved in various aspects of the project.{{Cite news |date=2023-04-16 |title=MTHL Project has domain experts from 10 countries and 14,000 skilled workers |work=The Times of India |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/mumbai/mthl-project-has-domain-experts-from-10-countries-and-14000-skilled-workers/articleshow/99527087.cms?from=mdr |access-date=2023-07-01 |issn=0971-8257}} [[Prime Minister of India|Prime Minister]] [[Narendra Modi]] laid the [[Cornerstone|foundation stone]] for the project on 24 December 2016.{{cite web|date=24 December 2016|title=Mumbai Trans Harbour Link: PM Narendra Modi lays foundation stone; 5 things to know about the mega project|url=http://www.financialexpress.com/india-news/mumbai-trans-harbour-link-5-things-to-know-about-the-project/485162/|access-date=13 January 2017|website=The Financial Express}} Construction of the MTHL began on 24 April 2018, with engineers collecting soil samples for soil testing at each location, where piers will be built in [[Nhava Sheva]].{{cite news|title=Work begins on trans-harbour link, company starts soil testing|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/mumbai/work-begins-on-trans-harbour-link-company-starts-soil-testing/articleshow/63903455.cms|website=The Times of India|date=25 April 2018 |access-date=11 May 2018}} The then MMRDA Metropolitan Commissioner, R. A. Rajeev, stated on 28 October 2018 that about 9% of the project work had been completed.{{cite web |title=9% of Mumbai Trans Harbour Link project completed |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/cities/mumbai/9-of-mumbai-trans-harbour-link-project-completed-5422597/ |website=The Indian Express |access-date=10 June 2019 |language=en-IN |date=29 October 2018}}{{cite news |title=Divers locate pipelines in sea as Mumbai trans-harbour project speeds up – Times of India |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/mumbai/divers-locate-pipelines-in-sea-as-mumbai-trans-harbour-project-speeds-up/articleshow/66407767.cms |website=The Times of India |date=29 October 2018 |access-date=11 November 2018}} The first pier of the MTHL was built at Sewri on 18 May 2019.{{cite news |last1=Mahale |first1=Ajeet |title=Trans harbour link's first pier comes up at Sewri |url=https://www.thehindu.com/news/cities/mumbai/trans-harbour-links-first-pier-comes-up-at-sewri/article27174882.ece |newspaper=The Hindu |access-date=10 June 2019 |language=en-IN |date=18 May 2019}} The MMRDA stated that it had begun pre-segment casting work, a precursor to the superstructure for bridge deck construction, on 7 August. Each segment of the viaduct weighs 75 tonnes with dimensions 14.8m x 3.32m x 3.85m. Over 10,000 such segments have been cast.{{cite web |title=Mumbai Trans Harbour Line commences work on pre-cast segment |url=https://www.devdiscourse.com/article/business/628618-mumbai-trans-harbour-line-commences-work-on-pre-cast-segment |website=Devdiscourse |access-date=11 August 2019 |language=en}} The segments were built at two precast segment yards, one on the Mumbai side and another on the Navi Mumbai side. The first segment was erected on the Sewri side about 6 km into the sea. MMRDA officials announced the completion of the pre-casting work on 9 August. Officials also stated that they had completed the construction of 270 permanent piles, of which 177 were in the sea. The agency had also completed the construction of a 2 km long temporary access bridge.{{cite news |last1=Aug 10 |first1=TNN {{!}} Updated |title=Mumbai's trans harbour link 75-tonne segment finished |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/mumbai/mumbai-trans-harbour-link-75-tonne-segment-finished/articleshow/70615686.cms |website=The Times of India |date=10 August 2019 |access-date=11 August 2019 |language=en}}{{cite web |title=Mumbai: MMRDA completes construction of the segment casting of MTHL |url=https://www.mid-day.com/articles/mumbai-mmrda-completes-construction-of-the-segment-casting-of-mthl/21512188 |website=mid-day |access-date=11 August 2019 |language=en |date=10 August 2019}} Casting for the first segment of Package 3 of the project began on 12 September 2019.{{cite web |title=Mumbai: MMRDA begins casting work for the first segment of package-3 of MTHL |url=https://www.mid-day.com/articles/mumbai-mmrda-begins-casting-work-for-the-first-segment-of-package-3-of-mthl/21723182 |website=mid-day |access-date=23 September 2019 |language=en |date=13 September 2019}} On the same date, MMRDA officials also stated that 20% of the total project work had been completed.{{cite web |title=MTHL set to be completed ahead of deadline |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/cities/mumbai/mthl-set-to-be-completed-ahead-of-deadline-5987356/ |website=The Indian Express |access-date=23 September 2019 |language=en-IN |date=12 September 2019}} The first girder, weighing 1,000 tonnes, for the MTHL was launched on 15 January 2020, marking the erection of its first span.{{Cite web|date=2020-01-15|title=Mumbai Trans Harbour Link: Uddhav Thackeray to launch first girder today|url=https://www.livemint.com/news/india/mumbai-trans-harbour-link-uddhav-thackeray-to-launch-first-girder-today-11579059759613.html|access-date=2021-11-25|website=mint|language=en}} The project faced delays due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]]. Over 5,000 workers had been deployed on the project before the pandemic, but this was reduced to around 2,000 workers by June 2020.{{cite web |title=Mumbai's infra dream takes a drastic hit in 2020 |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/mumbai-news/mumbai-s-infra-dream-takes-a-drastic-hit-in-2020/story-LLGtASue7dteDQnWjfxsHK.html |website=Hindustan Times |access-date=23 January 2021 |language=en |date=30 December 2020}} An estimated 27% of the total project work had been completed by June 2020,{{cite web |title=MMRDA plans green corridor along MTHL |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/mumbai-news/mmrda-plans-green-corridor-along-mthl/story-ix6tV3CSE5XLkvvEk5V11O.html |website=Hindustan Times |access-date=23 January 2021 |language=en |date=10 August 2020}} and 35.29% by November 2020.{{cite web |title=About 35% of Mumbai Trans Harbour Sealink project cost spent so far |url=https://www.freepressjournal.in/mumbai/about-35-of-mumbai-trans-harbor-sealink-project-cost-spent-so-far |website=Free Press Journal |language=en}} The [[Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation|BMC]] Tree Authority granted permission to the MMRDA to cut 454 trees and transplant another 550 trees for the MTHL project on 2 December 2020. The MMRDA stated that it would also plant 2,000 trees in [[Vasai]] to compensate for the loss.{{Cite web|author=Shashank Rao|date=3 December 2020|title=Mumbai Trans Harbour Link: 454 trees to face the axe to make way for the project|url=https://mumbaimirror.indiatimes.com/mumbai/civic/to-build-mthl-454-trees-to-face-the-axe/articleshow/79539244.cms|access-date=2021-11-25|website=Mumbai Mirror|language=en}} The agency stated that 40% of the total project work had been completed by the end of June 2021.{{Cite web|title=Mumbai: Nearly 40% of civil work completed in Mumbai Trans Harbour Link project|url=https://www.freepressjournal.in/mumbai/mumbai-nearly-40-of-civil-work-completed-in-mumbai-trans-harbour-link-project|access-date=2021-11-25|website=Free Press Journal|language=en}} The then Minister of State for Urban Development and Public Works, [[Eknath Shinde]]'s Public Relation Office, stated in August 2021 that 52% of the project work had been completed. The vision barriers are intended to block the view of the [[Bhabha Atomic Research Centre]] (BARC) from the MTHL, while the noise barriers are intended to protect the movement of flamingos and migratory birds at the Sewri mudflats. The MMRDA also stated that it would declare nearly 2 km of the MTHL on the Sewri side as a "silent zone", as well as near schools and other sensitive areas on the Navi Mumbai side of the MTHL.{{cite web |title=Obstructed sea view: 30% of Mumbai Trans Harbour Link to have noise & vision barriers |url=https://www.dnaindia.com/mumbai/report-obstructed-sea-view-30-of-mumbai-trans-harbour-link-to-have-noise-vision-barriers-2672849 |website=dna |access-date=15 October 2018 |date=8 October 2018}} Construction equipment used during the project was fitted with silencers to reduce the potential impact of noise on migratory birds such as flamingos. The project utilized reverse circulation drilling methodology, which helps reduce noise levels and helps speed up construction in marine areas.{{cite web|title=Mumbai Trans Harbour Link Project: Construction machines fitted with silencers to control noise level|url=https://www.freepressjournal.in/mumbai/mumbai-trans-harbour-link-project-construction-machines-fitted-with-silencers-to-control-noise-level|access-date=10 June 2019|website=Free Press Journal}} === Bird watching platform === A 5.6 km long temporary access bridge had been built to transport equipment and workers for the construction of the MTHL. In November 2021, the MMRDA announced that it had decided against demolishing the bridge and would convert it into a [[birdwatching]] platform to view flamingos and other birds. The agency noted that the decision would also save the cost of having to demolish the bridge.{{Cite web|date=2021-11-05|title=Temporary bridge built for construction of Mumbai harbour link to be retained as bird-watching platform|url=https://indianexpress.com/article/cities/mumbai/temporary-bridge-built-for-construction-of-mumbai-harbour-link-to-be-retained-as-bird-watching-platform-7607758/|access-date=2021-11-26|website=The Indian Express|language=en}} ===Traffic management and safety measures=== As a [[Controlled-access highway|access-controlled road]], to efficiently manage and regulate traffic movement across the MTHL, it has the Advanced Traffic Management System (ATMS), which is a centralised system that allows operators to monitor and manage traffic, incidents and emergency responses in real-time. Along with this, the Intelligent Transportation Management System (ITMS) is also present to systematically work with the ATMS together. This has given the bridge international recognition for having advanced systems to manage traffic.{{cite news|title=Steel used in Atal Setu can help build 4 Howrah Bridges, 17 Eiffel Towers — Here's all you need to know about MTHL sea bridge|url=https://indianexpress.com/article/cities/mumbai/steel-atal-setu-build-4-howrah-bridges-17-eiffel-towers-mthl-sea-bridge-9106845/|work=The Indian Express|date=12 January 2024|access-date=12 January 2024|language=en}} Similar to the [[Bandra–Worli Sea Link]], [[Coastal Road (Mumbai)|Coastal Road]] and the [[Eastern Freeway (Mumbai)|Eastern Freeway]], due to safety considerations, two-wheelers and three-wheelers are prohibited from entering the Trans Harbour Link, along with animal-drawn carriages and slow-moving vehicles. Although pedal and electric bicycles are prohibited as well, there are no signages or written warnings to enforce the ban, though riders can be penalized by law enforcement despite no provisions under [[Motor Vehicles Act]].{{Cite web|url= https://www.wionews.com/india-news/heres-why-no-autos-or-bikes-will-run-on-indias-longest-sea-bridge-678972|title= Atal Setu: Here's why no autos or bikes will run on India's longest sea bridge|date= 11 January 2024}} The traffic division of [[Mumbai Police]] has mandated a speed limit of 100 km/h (62 mph) to prevent fatalities. Furthermore, stopping on the bridge is prohibited, with the exception of emergencies, breakdowns, or when pulled over by law enforcement.{{Cite web|url= https://www.indiatoday.in/india/story/mumbai-trans-harbour-link-photos-videos-cost-mthl-traffic-rules-mumbai-police-2487221-2024-01-11|title= Speed limit 100 km/hr, no bikes and autos: All about India's longest sea bridge|date= 11 January 2024}} ===Technology and other features=== The structural steel used in the bridge is about 120,000 tonnes, enough to support the erection of four [[Howrah Bridge]]s. More than 830,000 cubic metres of concrete have been used to cast the structures of the bridge, which is six times more than the quantity used for building the [[Statue of Unity]]. The reinforced steel used is 17 times the quantity used in the [[Eiffel Tower]]. The bridge is constructed using corrosion-resistant materials to withstand weather variations, high wind speeds and tides, along with natural phenomena like earthquakes and cyclones. It can withstand earthquakes up to 6.5 magnitude, thus giving the lifespan of the bridge to remain intact for over a century. The 70 spans of [[Orthotropic deck|Orthotropic Steel Decks]] (OSDs) with lengths ranging from 65 to 180 metres and weighing up to 2,800 metric tons were erected across the [[Thane Creek]] using [[Science and technology in Japan|Japanese technology]]{{citation needed|date=November 2025}} In addition, a Comprehensive Surveillance System (CSS) utilizes a network of high-definition CCTV cameras strategically placed along the entire route. The Speed Violation Detection System (SVDS) has been installed to enforce speed limits and ensure enhanced road safety for commuters. A Video Incident Detection System (VIDS) that promptly detects and responds to incidents and mishaps has been installed. There are Emergency Calling Boxes (ECBs) on the bridge to provide commuters with a direct communication link to emergency services. Also, Variable Message Display (VMD) systems have been installed to effectively communicate and provide real-time information to commuters. ===Environmental safety and Sustainability measures=== The roads on both sides of the bridge have been paved with [[stone mastic asphalt]] (SMA) The bridge is paved with stone matrix asphalt, which has a high percentage of crushed, durable stone aggregates and a specialised asphalt binder. SMA increases the pavement life by 20–30% because of its high resistance to variations in temperature, better adhesion between the stone aggregate and [[bitumen]], reduces traffic noise, has high skid resistance and enhances [[road surface marking]] visibility. The surface will remain completely smooth and intact, irrespective of weather conditions. The SMA pavements will be 100% recyclable at the end of their service life, thus keeping the environment free of pollution. The [[carbon footprint]] from vehicular emissions will also significantly reduce by a few hundred thousand tons, as vehicles will be crossing the bridge at a maximum speed limit of {{cvt|100|km/h}}. Environmentalists were concerned that the lighting on the bridge would disturb marine life at night. To solve the issue, engineers have installed 1,212 special light poles that will illuminate only the carriageways, without any luminous spill onto the sea, thus positively affecting the marine life. These eco-friendly and sustainability measures have earned the bridge and the MMRDA a sustainability certificate from the [[Bombay Natural History Society]] (BNHS).{{cite news|title=Atal Setu (MTHL) opening today: 10 key points you need to know|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/mumbai/mumbai-trans-harbour-link-opening-10-key-highlights-you-need-to-know/articleshow/106723640.cms|work=The Times of India|date=12 January 2024|access-date=12 January 2024|language=en}} ==Cost== The cost of the MTHL has increased several times. Ambedkar|Ambedkar Road]], Elphinstone Bridge in [[Parel]], and the flyover at [[Pandurang Mahadev Bapat#Legacy|Senapati Bapat Marg]] before passing through Kamgar Nagar and Dr. Annie Besant Road, and terminating at Narayan Hardikar Marg at Worli.{{Cite web |date=2020-11-25 |title=4.5-km Sewri–Worli elevated corridor project for Mumbai Trans-Harbour Link awarded to contractor |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/mumbai-news/4-5-km-sewri-worli-elevated-corridor-project-for-mumbai-trans-harbour-link-awarded-to-contractor/story-H0ZjUolx0m6IFjamEim0JM.html |access-date=2021-11-26 |website=Hindustan Times |language=en}} Ramps will connect the Sewri–Worli elevated corridor with Rafi Ahmed Kidwai Marg, west of Sewri railway station, and with Acharya Donde Marg at Mumbai Port Trust.{{Cite web |title=MMRDA seeks contractor for design & construction of Sewri-Worli connector |url=https://www.freepressjournal.in/mumbai/mmrda-seeks-contractor-for-design-construction-of-sewri-worli-connector |access-date=2021-11-26 |website=Free Press Journal |language=en}} The Sewri–Worli connector was first proposed by the MMRDA in 2012–2013. The project was estimated to cost {{INRConvert|517|c|year=2014}}, and to be completed in four years.{{cite news |date=2014-01-15 |title=Lowest bidder likely to bag Worli–Sewri project |newspaper=The Indian Express |url=http://indianexpress.com/article/cities/mumbai/lowest-bidder-likely-to-bag-worli-sewri-project/ |access-date=2016-01-21}} The MMRDA received bids from 5 companies to construct the Sewri–Worli connector. They were Simplex Infrastructures Ltd., Larsen & Toubro, [[Hindustan Construction Company]] (HCC), Gammon India, and the National Construction Company (NCC). Simplex Infrastructures Ltd. quoted the lowest bid (nearly 16–17% below the estimated cost of the project), followed by Larsen & Toubro (14% below the reserve price).{{cite web |author=Ateeq Shaikh |date=2014-01-15 |title=5 firms bid for Sewri–Worli connector |url=http://www.dnaindia.com/mumbai/report-5-firms-bid-for-sewri-worli-connector-1951102 |access-date=2016-01-21 |website=Daily News and Analysis}} In April 2016, ''[[DNA (newspaper)|DNA]]'' reported that the project had been cancelled, after previously being put "on hold" in 2015. No budgetary allocation was made for the project in the 2015–16 fiscal year, and the MMRDA had no future plans to construct the connector.{{cite web |date=18 April 2016 |title=Maharashtra: MMRDA drops Sewri–Worli Elevated Road Connector project |url=http://www.dnaindia.com/mumbai/report-mmrda-drops-sewri-worli-elevated-road-connector-project-2203202 |access-date=18 April 2016 |website=dna |language=en-US}} The agency floated tenders again in 2017 at an estimated cost of {{INRConvert|1276|c}}. Apart from delays, the cost increase was also the result of some major design changes. The proposed connector will be built with a steel superstructure instead of cement as per the original plan. The MMRDA also proposed additional ramps to link the Sewri–Worli connector with Dr Rafi Ahmed Kidwai Marg, west of Sewri railway station, and with Acharya Donde Marg at Mumbai Port Trust. Further, the agency will demolish the existing single-tier road over bridge at Prabhadevi railway station and replace it with a new two-tier road over bridge. The agency later paused plans for the connector due to delays with the MTHL project.{{cite web |date=20 May 2019 |title=Mumbai: Cost of Sewri–Worli connector project doubled due to delay |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/cities/mumbai/mumbai-cost-of-sewri-worli-connector-project-doubled-due-to-delay-5736562/ |access-date=10 June 2019 |website=The Indian Express |language=en-IN}} The MMRDA floated new tenders for the project in July 2020. The project received clearance from the Maharashtra Coastal Zone Management Authority (MCZMA) on 7 July 2020, and from the Maharashtra State Environment Impact Assessment Authority (SEIAA) on 8 September 2020.{{cite news |title=Foundation stone laid for Sewri–Worli elevated connector, other key projects |url=https://www.constructionweekonline.in/projects-tenders/16744-foundation-stone-laid-for-sewri-worli-elevated-connector-other-key-projects |access-date=26 November 2021 |newspaper=Construction Week India|date=23 February 2021 }} J. Kumar Infraprojects Ltd. was awarded the contract to build the Sewri–Worli connector in November 2020. The project is estimated to cost {{INRConvert|1051.86|c}}. Construction began on 13 January 2021.{{Cite web |date=2022-10-21 |title=Changing City: Sewri–Worli connector to disperse traffic from upcoming Mumbai Trans Harbour Sealink |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/cities/mumbai/changing-city-sewri-worli-connector-upcoming-mumbai-trans-harbour-sealink-8223008/ |access-date=2022-12-06 |website=The Indian Express |language=en}} The then Chief Minister of Maharashtra, [[Uddhav Thackeray]], laid the foundation stone for the project on 21 February 2021.{{Cite web |title=Ahead of BMC polls, CM Thackeray lays foundation stone for Sewri–Worli elevated connector, launches key infra projects |url=https://www.mumbailive.com/en/infrastructure/ahead-of-bmc-polls-cm-thackeray-lays-foundation-stone-for-sewri-worli-elevated-connector-launches-key-infra-projects-61878 |access-date=2021-11-26 |website=Mumbai Live |date=22 February 2021 |language=en}} 25.77% of work on the project was completed by November 2022.{{Cite web |date=2022-10-21 |title=Changing City: Sewri–Worli connector to disperse traffic from upcoming Mumbai Trans Harbour Sealink |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/cities/mumbai/changing-city-sewri-worli-connector-upcoming-mumbai-trans-harbour-sealink-8223008/ |access-date=2023-07-01 |website=The Indian Express |language=en}} As of January 2024, 50% of work has been completed. It is expected to open by the end of 2024.{{cite news|last1=K. Mehta|first1=Manthan|last2=Nayak|first2=B. B.|title=22-km sea link: Gateway to a brave, new Mumbai|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/mumbai/22-km-sea-link-gateway-to-a-brave-new-mumbai/articleshow/106714452.cms|work=The Times of India|date=5 January 2024|access-date=5 January 2024|language=en}} === Shivajinagar interchange === The Shivajinagar interchange connects the MTHL with the [[Navi Mumbai International Airport]], [[Jawaharlal Nehru Port]], and local roads. It has been built to connect [[Ulwe]] directly to the MTHL through the planned Ulwe Coastal Road. Once the planned road is constructed, it will join this interchange at Shivajinagar.{{Cite news |date=2023-04-16 |title=How MTHL interchanges will bring Pune and Goa closer to Mumbai |work=The Times of India |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/mumbai/how-mthl-interchanges-will-bring-pune-and-goa-closer-to-mumbai/articleshow/99527540.cms?from=mdr |access-date=2023-07-01 |issn=0971-8257}} === Chirle interchange === The Chirle interchange connects the MTHL with the [[Mumbai–Pune Expressway]], and also provides connectivity to JNPT and [[Panvel]]. By joining the [[National Highway 348 (India)|NH-348]] at this point, it connects the MTHL with the expressway. But, to establish a direct link with the expressway, to decrease the increasing traffic demand and congestion to and from [[Pune]], the MTHL will be extended from this interchange to link with it near the under-construction [[Navi Mumbai International Airport]], which is also proposed to be connected with the help of an airport connector road.{{Cite web |date=2023-03-09 |title=To ease traffic, MTHL road to be connected to Mumbai-Pune Expressway: MMRDA |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/cities/mumbai-news/mumbai-trans-harbour-link-to-be-connected-with-mum-pun-eway-101678301912328.html |access-date=2023-07-01 |website=Hindustan Times |language=en}} ==Toll== In 2012, the MMRDA proposed tolls for the MTHL as {{INR}}175 for cars, {{INR}}265 for light commercial vehicles, {{INR}}525 for buses and trucks, and {{INR}}790 for multi-axle vehicles. JICA, the primary source of funding for the project, proposed higher tolls in 2016.{{Cite web | url=http://www.asianage.com/mumbai/pay-more-mthl-toll-789 |title = Pay more for MTHL toll|date = 2 March 2016}} The toll rates levied after the project opened was expected to be much higher due to cost escalations.{{cite web|title=MTHL: With increasing civil cost, toll burden set to go up {{!}} Latest News & Updates at Daily News & Analysis|url=http://www.dnaindia.com/mumbai/report-mthl-with-increasing-civil-cost-toll-burden-set-to-go-up-2561667|website=dna|access-date=11 May 2018|date=22 November 2017}} In January 2024, after the opening of the MTHL, the [[Government of Maharashtra]] revised the toll rates from former rates as ₹ 200 for cars for one way from Mumbai to Navi Mumbai, a reduction from the initial plans of ₹ 500 and ₹ 250, and ₹ 300 from Navi Mumbai to Mumbai for return journeys, ₹ 320 and ₹ 480 for buses, ₹ 655 and ₹ 985 for [[light commercial vehicle]]s (LCVs), ₹ 715 and ₹ 1075 for trucks, ₹ 1030 and ₹ 1545 for heavy-duty trucks and ₹ ₹ 1255 and ₹ 1885 for oversized vehicles. All vehicles are allowed to travel through the bridge, except two-wheelers, tractors, small, very light to light commercial vehicles and [[auto-rickshaw]]s. The toll rates will be consistently decreased further over time as the MTHL caters to more vehicles.{{cite news|title=PM Modi inaugurates Mumbai Trans Harbour Link: Who can use it, who can't?|url=https://www.firstpost.com/explainers/pm-inaugurates-indias-longest-sea-bridge-mumbai-trans-harbour-link-who-can-use-it-who-cant-13606332.html|work=Firstpost|date=12 January 2024|access-date=12 January 2024|language=en}} The toll collection is done with an [[Open road tolling]] (ORT) system, present on the Navi Mumbai side of the bridge, which does not involve the stopping of vehicular movement at a toll booth and manually collecting tolls. Instead, specialized cameras installed under a shed scan vehicles passing through without having to halt, and automatically obtain tolls. Such a system not only helps commuters to be free of traffic and congestion, but also eliminates long queues, risk of mishaps, reduces pollution and the risk of un-organized collection of tolls, and ensures free flow of traffic, fuel efficiency, low carbon footprint and other benefits.{{Cite web |date=12 January 2023 |title=India's longest sea bridge in Mumbai will be open for traffic in November |url=https://www.thehindu.com/news/cities/mumbai/indias-longest-sea-bridge-in-mumbai-will-be-open-for-traffic-in-november/article66369834.ece/ |url-status=live The Mumbai Trans Harbour Link, officially named as Atal Bihari Vajpayee Sewri–Nhava Sheva Atal Setu and colloquially known as Atal Setu, is a 18.2 km (11.3 mi), 6-lane grade separated expressway bridge, which connects Mumbai with Navi Mumbai, its satellite city. It is the longest sea bridge in India, and the world's 12th longest sea bridge. The bridge begins in Sewri, South Mumbai, crosses Thane Creek north of Elephanta Island, and terminates at Chirle near Nhava Sheva in Uran taluka, South Navi Mumbai. The road is linked to NH348 in the east and to the Eastern Freeway in the west.
The 6-lane highway is 27 meters in width, in addition to two emergency exit lanes, two edge strips, parallel crash barriers and noise barriers on both sides. The project costs a total of ₹17,843 crore (US$1.9 billion). The bridge has a capacity to handle 70,000 vehicles per day. Construction on the bridge began in April 2018, and was inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on 12 January 2024.
